guia.what: Persistent side navigation. It collapses to an icon rail or hides completely, remembers its state, and turns into a Drawer on its own below `lg`. Shortcut: `⌘/Ctrl + B`.
whenUse: There are many sections, with hierarchy, and keeping them always visible helps.
Users jump between sections often (docs, an admin dashboard).
You want the same navigation to become a panel on small screens.
whenAvoid: There are only a few sections, and they fit at the top → `nav-bar`.
It’s the table of contents for the page being read → `toc`.
It’s a temporary panel that opens and closes → `drawer`.
dos: Group items by topic and mark the active one.
Let it collapse. On small screens, the content matters more than the menu.
In the collapsed rail, the items of an expanded group stay as icons, so give each item its own. A collapsed group is not reachable until the bar is expanded.
donts: Don’t nest menus three levels deep. It turns into a maze.
Don’t duplicate what’s already in the top bar.

teclado.action: In the collapsed rail, Tab moves through the items shown as icons, and Enter activates the focused one.

nucleo: It’s a set of parts (bar, groups, items, trigger) that coordinate with each other. Collapses and expands with persistence, supports nested groups, and marks the active item. Below the breakpoint (`data-ts-breakpoint`, via `@media`), the bar hides, and the HTML includes the Drawer with the same navigation. The trigger (`data-ts-sidebar-trigger`) opens it in a narrow viewport and collapses the bar in a wide one. If you widen the viewport with the Drawer open, it closes and focus returns to the trigger.
